finding: The live range of $180-$675 is about right at the bottom and too low at the top for a job done with genuine parts at an ordinary shop time. Built totals use parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr (the national middle labor rate used for these checks), for one front door regulator with its motor. Economy, 2013 Honda Civic sedan: $84.95 aftermarket assembly to $401.49 genuine regulator plus motor, + 0.4-2.5 hr = about $133-$801. Midsize, 2020 Subaru Outback: only the genuine assembly was priced, $317.93 list + 0.4-2.5 hr = about $366-$718 (about $265-$617 at the discounted online price of $217.47). Truck/SUV, 2022 Dodge Durango: $149.40 to $354.56 + 1.2-2.5 hr = about $293-$755. Luxury, 2015 BMW 328i: $234.36 to $515.38 + 1.0-2.5 hr = about $354-$915. The very lowest total, about $133, needs the cheapest aftermarket assembly and Honda's 0.4 hr warranty time; at the 1.5 hr that a general repair guide gives as the low end of shop time, the same Civic job is about $265-$325, so a $180 floor is reasonable for a cheap part on an easy car. The top is the problem: with genuine parts and 2.5 hr every example passes $675 (about $718 to $915), and even at 1.5 hr the BMW with genuine parts is about $695-$755. RepairPal's national average ($421-$566) sits inside the live range; Jerry ($138-$204) and J.D. Power ($200-$300) describe cheaper regulator-only or motor-only jobs. What is null and why: the aftermarket (low) price for the 2020 Outback; the aftermarket assemblies found were for the 2015-2019 or 2010-2014 cars, so that class rests on one priced source. Parts caveats: Honda, Mopar and BMW sell the regulator and the motor as separate parts, so those figures add two list prices, and a shop may replace only the failed one; the Civic's genuine driver-door motor ($243.32) costs far more than the passenger one ($97.53), so the passenger door comes to $245.87 at list. The Durango low mixes an aftermarket regulator ($49.95) with a genuine motor at a discounted online price ($99.45) because no aftermarket motor price was loaded, and the genuine motor's list price was read from the 2021 Durango page (same part number). The BMW aftermarket motor carries a refundable core charge that is not included. How solid the labor times are: the low ends for the economy, midsize and truck/SUV classes are manufacturer warranty times printed in dealer bulletins for the example vehicles themselves (Honda 0.4-0.5 hr for one front regulator and motor on the 2012-2013 Civic; Subaru 0.4 hr for one motor and regulator assembly on the 2020 Outback; FCA 1.2 hr to inspect, reseat and replace one regulator on the 2022-2023 Durango). Warranty times are the low end of what shops bill. The truck/SUV example is a three-row SUV because no full-size pickup bulletin with a printed regulator time was found. The luxury class has no manufacturer-stated time at all: its hours are general guide figures, not vehicle-specific. All high ends rest on one general repair guide's statement of 1.5-2.5 hours at a shop or dealer, supported by Jerry's 1-2 hours and J.D. Power's 2.1-hour average for a motor; J.D. Power also says some vehicles reach four to five hours. The Honda and Subaru times are for regulator and motor together, matching the unit; the FCA bulletins do not say whether the motor is included. An estimate is never a quote and never a diagnosis.
extras: A quote often adds a diagnosis fee (a dead window can also be a switch, fuse, wiring in the door jamb or a door module), door panel clips and a vapor barrier or sealant, window re-initialization or module programming on one-touch windows, shop supplies and sales tax. If the glass has dropped or come out of its channel, glass, run channel or clips may be added. Some vehicles sell the regulator and motor separately and a shop may replace only the failed one; the other side is quoted separately.
